report.summary: Reviewed chunk 3 of gated_writes.py: claims in _PinnedWorktreeGit, _reattempt, _as_cancel_predicate, _CumulativeGateCancelled, _promote_one_inner docstrings/comments verified against code.
risks: _PinnedWorktreeGit.run | medium | --git-dir/--work-tree flags are passed BEFORE -c config overrides; if git treats later -c as overriding earlier command-line options, the no-op config values could override the pinned dirs, breaking the pin. | Check git's option precedence for -c vs --git-dir.

_promote_one_inner | medium | Re-gate runs with test_cwd forced to '.', but project config may legitimately require a different cwd; the code raises and aborts the promotion instead of adapting. | Inspect project config expectations and whether test_cwd is always '.'.

_promote_one_inner | low | Cancellation is only honoured while the test command runs; the commit step just before it is not cancellable and could be slow on large repos. | Assess commit performance and whether a stop request during commit is acceptable.

_as_cancel_predicate | low | Broken callable/event treated as 'not cancelled' could let a long test run to completion even when the caller's token is genuinely broken; the docstring justifies this as safe, but it may surprise a caller expecting cancellation. | Review caller expectations for broken cancellation tokens.

handoff.purpose: Verify claims in _PinnedWorktreeGit, _reattempt, _as_cancel_predicate, _CumulativeGateCancelled, and _promote_one_inner against the code in this chunk.

symbols.name: _GIT_EXEC_CONFIG
symbols.note: Tuple of git -c config overrides used to harden git execution.

symbols.name: _hardened_env
symbols.note: Builds a copy of os.environ with git security overrides and strips leaky git variables.

symbols.name: _read_gitdir_pointer
symbols.note: Reads a worktree's .git pointer once; returns Path for dir or gitdir: target, None on failure.

symbols.name: _PinnedWorktreeGit
symbols.note: Runs git commands pinned to the admin dir captured at construction.

symbols.name: _PinnedWorktreeGit.__init__
symbols.note: Stores worktree and captures admin_dir via _read_gitdir_pointer.

symbols.name: _PinnedWorktreeGit.run
symbols.note: Spawns git with pinned dirs, config overrides, hardened env; raises RuntimeError on non-zero exit if check=True.

symbols.name: _reattempt
symbols.note: Re-runs a candidate's spec against a new base revision via run_attempt and returns a new GatedCandidate.

symbols.name: _as_cancel_predicate
symbols.note: Normalises a cancel token to a zero-arg predicate; broken callables/events return False.

symbols.name: _CumulativeGateCancelled
symbols.note: RuntimeError subclass raised when the cumulative re-gate is cancelled, distinct from ordinary gate failure.

symbols.name: _promote_one_inner
symbols.note: Promotes a single candidate: regenerates on staleness, applies patch, commits, runs cumulative test gate.

claims.text: Mirrors daedalus.spine.attempt._read_gitdir_pointer (private there, reimplemented here rather than imported).
claims.why: The mirrored function is in another module; this chunk cannot compare implementations.

claims.text: the pointer is read ONCE, at construction -- callers must construct this immediately after create_worktree and before the first git apply -- and every subsequent call is pinned to that captured path explicitly, never re-resolved from the (by-then possibly candidate-controlled) working tree.
claims.why: __init__ captures admin_dir once; run uses it for --git-dir/--work-tree on every invocation, never re-reading .git from the worktree.

claims.text: a candidate-authored .gitattributes spawn an arbitrary program via a config-bound filter/textconv driver
claims.why: This is historical evidence from attempt.py's history; not observable in this chunk.

claims.text: Re-run the SAME instruction/target_paths against a NEW base commit.
claims.why: fresh_spec = _dc_replace(candidate.spec, base_revision=new_base) preserves all other spec fields, so instruction and target_paths are unchanged.

claims.text: A fresh TaskSpec (same content, new base_revision) through the same TaskAttempt/offload_runner path as Phase 1: no new isolation mechanism, just the existing one invoked again with an updated base.
claims.why: It builds runner_kwargs, uses _recording_runner, and calls run_attempt with the same parameters as Phase 1 (as described in the codebase).

claims.text: cancel is forwarded unchanged to this regeneration's own TaskAttempt
claims.why: run_attempt is called with cancel=cancel, passing the same object through.

claims.text: Same three-way contract as the original: None -> never cancelled; a callable -> called, a broken callable treated as 'not cancelled' (a token that raises must not be able to abort work it was only supposed to observe); anything exposing is_set() (a threading.Event, a KillSwitch) -> that, same broken-token rule.
claims.why: The function returns lambda: False for None, wraps callables and is_set() in try/except returning False on exception, and raises TypeError for anything else.

claims.text: Deliberately NOT an import of daedalus.spine.attempt._as_predicate
claims.why: The existence and privacy of daedalus.spine.attempt._as_predicate cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: the SAME fabricated-verdict shape this repo already fixed once -- a cooperative stop reported as an ordinary gate failure -- cannot recur here
claims.why: The historical fix is external; this chunk cannot verify it.

claims.text: the except block below still resets the integration worktree exactly as it does for a real failure (that reset is unconditional and was already safe for cancellation before this class existed -- see the comment on that reset)
claims.why: The except block in _promote_one_inner catches Exception and resets the worktree unconditionally (as seen in the code); the comment on that reset is present.

claims.text: the REASON string a caller sees now says cancelled, not gate failed
claims.why: When gate_result.cancelled, the code raises _CumulativeGateCancelled with message starting 'cumulative gate cancelled'; for non-cancelled failures it raises RuntimeError with 'cumulative gate failed'.

claims.text: Bounded to ONE retry -- a second staleness hit means something is landing candidates faster than this one can be recomputed, which is a reason to stop and report, not to loop.
claims.why: If artifact.base_revision != current_head and _retried is True, it returns immediately with retried: True; otherwise it recurses with _retried=True, so at most one regeneration.

claims.text: NOTHING WRITTEN. git apply (no --3way, no --reject) validates the whole patch before writing anything; a non-zero exit here means the integration worktree is exactly as it was before this call.
claims.why: git apply without --3way/--reject is atomic: it checks the whole patch before applying; a non-zero return means no changes were made. The code returns immediately without further mutation.

claims.text: Refused and reported, never retried with a fuzzier match and never merged with conflict markers.
claims.why: On apply failure, the code returns a failure dict with reason; there is no retry or merge logic.

claims.text: cumulative re-gate needs test_cwd='.'; project configures {test_cwd!r}
claims.why: The code raises RuntimeError if test_cwd is not in (None, '', '.'), explicitly requiring '.'.

claims.text: WAS `lambda: False` (uncancellable) -- this is the one gate in the promote path that runs the project's WHOLE test command, so it is the longest-running thing a stop request can land inside.
claims.why: The claim about prior state and being the longest-running gate depends on other promote-path code not in this chunk.

claims.text: Safe to make cancellable: the `except` block just below already resets the integration worktree to `current_head` unconditionally on ANY failure here, cancellation included, so honouring `cancel` adds no new way to leave that worktree in a worse state than finishing would -- it only shortens how long a stop takes to land.
claims.why: The except block catches Exception and resets the worktree unconditionally (as seen in the code); the reset is to current_head (as described in the comment).

claims.text: Distinct exception type on purpose -- see _CumulativeGateCancelled's own docstring: the reason string a caller reads back must say 'cancelled', never 'gate failed', or this reintroduces the exact fabricated-verdict shape this parameter exists to close.
claims.why: The code raises _CumulativeGateCancelled with 'cumulative gate cancelled' and RuntimeError with 'cumulative gate failed' for the two cases, so the reason strings are distinct.

observations.what: _PinnedWorktreeGit.run passes --git-dir/--work-tree before the -c config overrides; if git gives -c precedence over command-line options, the config overrides could override the pinned dirs.

_reattempt imports run_attempt from daedalus.spine.attempt, but the module already has offload_runner imported; the docstring says 'same TaskAttempt/offload_runner path as Phase 1' and the code uses run_attempt directly, which is consistent with the described path.
The cumulative re-gate forces test_cwd='.', but project config may legitimately require a different cwd; the code raises and aborts the promotion instead of adapting.
Cancellation is only honoured while the test command runs; the commit step just before it is not cancellable and could be slow on large repos.

_as_cancel_predicate treats a broken callable/event as 'not cancelled', which could let a long test run to completion even when the caller's token is genuinely broken; the docstring justifies this as safe, but it may surprise a caller expecting cancellation.
